original_question: Fix chi < 1. Is there a constant C'_chi > 0 such that for every N, at least chi N^d choices of (a_1, ..., a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N produce the d-dimensional lattice point set (({n a_1 / N}, ..., {n a_d / N}))_{n=0}^{N-1} whose discrepancy D_N is at least C'_chi (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Open Problem 1: the average-type lower-bound problem for d-dimensional lattice point sets, posed immediately after Theorem 2.7.
correct_elements: The draft identifies the correct class of objects (the d-dimensional lattice/rank-1 lattice point sets generated by a vector a modulo N), the correct proportion statement (at least chi N^d generator vectors), the correct order of magnitude for the desired lower bound ((log N)^(d-1) log log N / N), and the correct quantifier over all N. It also asks for the lower-bound counterpart of the upper average-type result stated just before the open problem.
missing_details: The ambient dimension d should be fixed explicitly; in a stand-alone formulation the constant should be allowed to depend on d as well as on chi.
The natural nontrivial range of the proportion parameter should be stated as 0 < chi < 1, not merely chi < 1.
The discrepancy symbol should be defined for this finite N-point set; the paper speaks of the discrepancy of the point set, not of an undefined D_N symbol.
The ambient space [0,1)^d and the fact that discrepancy is taken with respect to axis-parallel half-open boxes/subintervals should be stated.
The generator vectors should be quantified as a = (a_1,...,a_d) in {0,1,...,N-1}^d.
It should be made explicit that the point set is indexed by n = 0,...,N-1.
No coprimality condition is imposed on the coordinates a_i (or on gcd(a_1,...,a_d,N)); the count is over all N^d choices.
Because no coprimality is assumed, the N listed points may repeat; the question concerns the discrepancy of that resulting N-point multiset/list.
To stay paper-faithful, the point set should be described as the finite analogue of a Kronecker sequence/good lattice point set from the introduction and Section 2 context.
The dependence of the sought constant on N must be excluded explicitly.
refined_question: Fix an integer d >= 2 and a real number chi with 0 < chi < 1. Does there exist a constant C_{d,chi} > 0 such that for every positive integer N, at least chi N^d vectors a = (a_1,...,a_d) in {0,1,...,N-1}^d have the property that the N-point lattice set P_N(a) = {({n a_1 / N},...,{n a_d / N}) : n = 0,1,...,N-1} subset [0,1)^d satisfies D(P_N(a)) >= C_{d,chi} (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N, where D(P_N(a)) denotes the usual discrepancy of this finite point set with respect to axis-parallel half-open boxes in [0,1)^d?
justification: The draft is aiming at Open Problem 1 in Section 2, not at Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3. Open Problem 1 is posed exactly as the lower-bound analogue of Theorem 2.7 for the same family of lattice point sets and with the same order ((log N)^(d-1) log log N)/N. The nearby context in the introduction supplies the underlying point-set model and the meaning of discrepancy, while Theorem 2.7 supplies the matching upper average-type statement that the open problem is meant to complement.
